spec_family.name: New Construction Interior Window Stain/Clear Coat
spec_family.description: Covers stain application, sanding sealer, and clear topcoat for interior window sash and jamb assemblies in new construction. Combined spec with coating_type dimension (stain_clear, stain_only, clear_only). Stain phase includes wipe step for all methods. Sealer and clear phases use independent application method selection. Uses EA as primary UOM with window_type and size_bucket modifiers. Material systems are product-role-based recommendations shared across all interior stain specs. Context prefix WIST avoids collision with WIN (paint counterpart SF_WINDOW_INT_NC).

includes: Stain application on bare wood window sash (brush+wipe, roll+wipe, spray+wipe)
Stain application on bare wood extension jamb/reveal (brush+wipe, roll+wipe, spray+wipe)
Sanding sealer application (0-2 coats, QT-driven defaults)
Clear topcoat application (1-3 coats, QT-driven defaults)
Bare wood preparation (inspect, sand 120-150 grit, fill defects with wood filler, grain raise for waterborne, tack clean)
Wood conditioner application (softwood + stain, unless gel stain)
Interstage sanding between sealer coats (220-320 grit)
Interstage sanding between clear coats (320-400 grit)
Stain dry verification before sealer/clear application
Glass masking (mandatory regardless of application method)
Floor protection below window work area
Wall masking around window (spray, or when walls are SS_PAINTED_*)
Hardware protection (remove or mask: locks, latches, crank operators)
Window sash stain/clear coat (double-hung, casement, fixed, awning)

excludes.item: Window casing stain/clear coat (exterior trim around window opening)
Interior repaint stain (stripping existing finish, recoating)

excludes.route_to: Out of scope — vinyl not stainable

configuration_dimensions.description: Primary configuration dimension — drives layer stack, material systems, and module activation. stain_clear is the full stain + sealer + clear workflow. stain_only applies stain without topcoat. clear_only applies clear without stain (natural wood or pre-stained).
configuration_dimensions.notes: stain_clear is the professional standard for interior window staining. stain_only is rare (unprotected stain). clear_only for natural wood look or pre-stained surfaces.

configuration_dimensions.description: Quality tier controlling inspection scrutiny, sanding discipline, and coat count defaults. Does NOT affect application quality (binary at all tiers).
configuration_dimensions.notes: QT3=budget (1 stain + 0 sealer + 1 clear = 2 coats). QT4=standard (1 stain + 1 sealer + 2 clear = 4 coats). QT5=premium (1 stain + 2 sealer + 3 clear = 6 coats). All coat counts user-overridable.

configuration_dimensions.description: Stain application technique. All stain methods include a wipe step to control color depth.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Brush is default for window detail work — sash brush gives best control in muntin and profile areas. Roll feasible for jamb areas. Spray for production volume. All methods include wipe-back step.

configuration_dimensions.description: Clear coat application technique. No roll option — causes air bubbles in clear coat.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Brush is default for control on window profiles. Spray for production volume. Roll PROHIBITED for clear coat (air bubble defects). Lacquer clear requires spray.

configuration_dimensions.description: Clear coat sheen. Drives product selection. Not applicable for stain_only.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Satin is most popular for residential windows. No sheen/QT gate — all sheens available at all tiers (unlike paint specs).

configuration_dimensions.description: Number of stain coats. User-selectable with default of 1.
configuration_dimensions.notes: 1 coat is standard. 2 coats for deeper color saturation. Default 1 at all QT levels.

configuration_dimensions.description: Number of sanding sealer coats. User-selectable with QT-driven defaults.
configuration_dimensions.notes: QT3 skips sealer (budget). QT4 uses 1 coat. QT5 uses 2 coats for maximum film build. All user-overridable.

configuration_dimensions.description: Number of clear topcoats. User-selectable with QT-driven defaults.
configuration_dimensions.notes: QT3 uses 1 coat (budget). QT4 uses 2 coats (standard). QT5 uses 3 coats (maximum protection and depth).

configuration_dimensions.description: Window operating type. Controls base production rate modifier.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Double-hung is baseline (most complex — two operable sashes). Casement simpler (single sash). Fixed simplest (no operable parts). Modifiers reflect relative complexity for stain/clear work.

configuration_dimensions.description: Window size category per PaintScope Size Bucket Method.
configuration_dimensions.notes: S=small (~8 LF perimeter), M=medium (~12 LF, baseline), L=large (~17 LF), XL=oversized (>20 LF). Modifiers scale production rates.

configuration_dimensions.description: Wood species grouping. Drives wood conditioner activation for softwood.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Softwood (pine, poplar, alder) requires pre-stain wood conditioner to prevent blotchy absorption — unless gel stain is selected (gel stain controls blotch inherently). Hardwood (oak, maple, cherry, walnut) does not need conditioner.

paintable_items.name: Window sash (frame + sash assembly)
paintable_items.counting_rules: Count each window opening as one EA. Includes frame interior face and operable sash(es) as a single assembly. Counted by size bucket (S/M/L/XL) and window type.
paintable_items.notes: Primary paintable item. EA-based with Size Bucket Method for rate scaling. Window type modifier applies per window. Stain wipe step is per-window operation.

paintable_items.name: Extension jamb / reveal
paintable_items.counting_rules: Same count as ITM_WINDOW_SASH — one extension jamb per window opening. May not be present on all windows (some have no extension jamb).
paintable_items.notes: Separate item because extension jamb may have different prep requirements (deeper reveal, different access angle). Same size bucket modifiers apply.

variants.notes: Budget stain+clear. 1 stain + 1 clear = 2 total coats. No sealer. Fastest clear workflow.
Standard stain+clear. 1 stain + 1 sealer + 2 clear = 4 total coats. Professional residential standard.
Premium stain+clear. 1 stain + 2 sealer + 3 clear = 6 total coats. Maximum film build and depth.
Production variant. Brush stain (control on profiles) + spray clear (finish quality). Common NC production workflow.
Stain-only, no clear coat. Minimal workflow — stain + wipe only. Unprotected finish.
Clear-only on natural or pre-stained wood. 1 sealer + 2 clear = 3 coats. No stain application.
Premium all-spray. Maximum production speed at highest quality tier. Full protection required.
Premium clear-only spray. 2 sealer + 3 clear = 5 coats. Lacquer-compatible variant.

required_paintscope_inputs.description: Count of window sash assemblies to stain/clear coat

required_paintscope_inputs.required_when: When extension jambs are present and in scope
required_paintscope_inputs.description: Count of extension jamb/reveals to stain/clear coat
Total glass area for masking — mandatory
Floor protection area below window work zone

required_paintscope_inputs.required_when: application_method_stain = spray OR application_method_clear = spray, or walls SS_PAINTED_*
required_paintscope_inputs.description: Wall masking LF around window perimeter
Window hardware groups for protection (locks, latches, operators) — mandatory

required_paintscope_inputs.required_when: application_method_clear = spray AND stool is SS_PAINTED_*
required_paintscope_inputs.description: Sill edge masking LF during spray

protection_zones_required.condition: ALWAYS — mandatory regardless of application method
protection_zones_required.notes: Paper/film masking on all window glass panes. Mandatory. Stain on glass is difficult to remove. Extra care needed vs paint — stain penetrates porous glass edges.
Drop cloths below window work area. Stain drips are especially difficult to clean from finished floors.
Tape/bag or remove window hardware (locks, latches, crank operators). Removal preferred — stain penetrates and is hard to clean from hardware.
Wall masking around window perimeter for spray method. Also required for any method when walls are SS_PAINTED_*.
Protect stool/sill from overspray. Only when stool is already finished (SS_PAINTED_*).

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Window frame meets wall at perimeter. Stain on walls is very difficult to clean — protection especially important.
Window casing handled by SF_TRIM_NC_STAIN. Often stained in same session with same stain/clear.
Stool handled by SF_TRIM_NC_STAIN. Often same stain finish. When already finished, protect from overspray.
Glass is NOT stained. Glass masking mandatory. Stain on glass is harder to remove than paint — careful masking critical.

valid_input_states.notes: Bare wood is the primary input state. clear_only also accepts SS_STAINED (pre-stained wood needing topcoat only). SS_CLEAR_COATED as input is RP scope.

output_state.notes: stain_clear and clear_only produce SS_CLEAR_COATED. stain_only produces SS_STAINED (unprotected).

adjacent_state_protection_rules.notes: When walls are finished (SS_PAINTED_*), wall masking around window required for ALL methods. Stain is harder to clean off painted walls than paint is.
When walls are unfinished, spray method still requires wall masking.
When walls are unfinished and non-spray method, no wall protection needed.

site_condition_rules.effect: Floor protection excluded when floor is subfloor.
site_condition_rules.notes: NC often has subfloor during window staining. Finished/partial floors require drop cloths below window area.

site_condition_rules.effect: Height modifier applies for elevated windows. H2=1.30 for 9-12ft, H3=1.50 for 13ft+.
site_condition_rules.notes: Per Modifier_Registry. Standard height windows have no height modifier.

sequencing_notes.production_sequence: Window staining typically occurs BEFORE wall finishing in NC sequence. Staining requires bare wood — cannot stain over primed or painted windows.
sequencing_notes.coat_sequence: Setup → Prep (sand, fill, grain raise, condition) → Stain coat 1 (+wipe) → [Stain coat 2] → Stain dry → Sealer coat 1 → [Sealer interstage → Sealer coat 2] → Sealer sand → Clear coat 1 → [Clear interstage → Clear coat 2] → [Clear coat 3] → Final inspect → Cleanup
sequencing_notes.protection_sequence: Glass masking (mandatory, first) → Floor protection → Hardware protection → Wall masking (if applicable) → Apply coats → Teardown
sequencing_notes.dry_times: Stain: 4-8 hrs (oil), 2 hrs (waterborne) before sealer/clear. Sealer: 2-4 hrs between coats. Clear: 4-6 hrs between coats (oil poly), 2 hrs (WB poly).
sequencing_notes.blocking_prevention: All operable sashes must remain AJAR during clear coat cure (3-7 days). Do NOT close — clear coat will bond sash to frame.
sequencing_notes.notes: Unlike paint specs, stain has no companion prime spec — bare wood prep and all coating layers in one spec.

relationships.notes: Stain counterpart to SF_WINDOW_INT_NC. Window stain often done in same session as trim stain (SF_TRIM_NC_STAIN). Shared material systems.

change_log.author: SpecFactory
change_log.changes: Initial draft spec for NC interior window stain/clear coat (Tier 3 in interior stain spec rollout). Key features: coating_type dimension (stain_clear/stain_only/clear_only), 2 paintable items (sash EA, jamb EA), independent stain and clear application methods, window_type modifier (double_hung/casement/fixed/awning), size_bucket modifier (S/M/L/XL), mandatory glass masking, blocking prevention for operable sashes, shared 9 material systems, 14 SOP modules, context prefix WIST.
